finding.claim: HIGH: the unauthenticated POST /hooks/test handler sends an HTTP POST to a URL taken from the request body, with no allowlist. The attacker can target internal hosts, loopback or cloud metadata (169.254.169.254), and axios follows redirects by default. Only the response status is returned, so this is semi-blind, but status codes still allow internal port and host probing. The router `pub` is not mounted in the audited files. The 'public' label comes from the name and the lack of auth middleware, so confirm the mounting.

trace.note: pub.post('/hooks/test') handler; no auth middleware on the pub router
req.body.callback passed directly as the URL to axios.post
r.status returned to the caller, which gives an oracle for internal probing

finding.guards_checked: No scheme or hostname allowlist, no URL parsing, and no IP/RFC-1918 blocking. No maxRedirects: 0, so redirects are followed. `requireAdmin` is applied only to the `admin` router (line 12), not to `pub`. No mount point or app file exists in the directory, so the auth state of `pub` is inferred.

verdict.reason: routes.js:19-21 passes req.body.callback straight into axios.post and returns r.status. No validation or auth applies, because requireAdmin is only attached to the `admin` router at routes.js:12. The `pub` router's mount point is not in the directory, so its exposure is inferred from the absence of auth middleware.

finding.claim: MEDIUM: the admin-only GET /diagnostics/fetch handler issues a GET to a URL from the query string, with no allowlist. An admin can reach internal services or cloud metadata, which goes beyond admin scope, and redirects are followed. Only the status is returned. Severity is MEDIUM rather than HIGH because the route requires an admin session. The skill's rule that admin-only access does not close SSRF to metadata or RFC-1918 applies.
finding.source: req.query.url (query-string parameter, attacker-controlled by an admin user or via a hijacked admin session)

trace.note: admin.use(requireAdmin) gates the router on session.role === 'admin'

finding.guards_checked: requireAdmin (routes.js:7-10) checks req.session.role === 'admin'. It does not restrict the destination. No URL allowlist, no scheme check, no IP blocking, and redirects are followed. The admin role does not demonstrably imply OS-level server access.

verdict.guard_found: requireAdmin (routes.js:7-10, applied at routes.js:12) restricts access to session.role === 'admin'. It does not restrict the destination URL, so it is not a closing guard for the sink itself.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (routes.js:12-16), but req.query.url at routes.js:15 is reachable only through the admin-gated router (routes.js:12, requireAdmin at routes.js:8), so under the stated source criteria it is not controllable by an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker; the unauthenticated-style sink at routes.js:20 (pub POST /hooks/test) is a separate finding.
